headline: Chromosome-scale and haplotype-phased genome assemblies across fungi and plants
label: Chromosome Level Genome Assemblies
summary: Long-read and chromosome-conformation sequencing now yields near chromosome-scale references for diverse non-model plant and fungal species.
synthesis: The four items share a common thread: long-read sequencing combined with chromosome-conformation data to produce highly contiguous reference genomes for non-model organisms. The two Melampsora poplar rust fungi are reported as haplotype-phased, near chromosome-scale assemblies built from HiFi and Hi-C reads. Oryza granulata, a shade-tolerant wild rice, is presented as a 764 Mb chromosome-scale reference with scaffold N50 near 59 Mb, BUSCO completeness of about 98.6%, and roughly 42,000 protein-coding genes. The Tropaeolum tuberosum tetraploid accession is assembled from PacBio HiFi reads to 1.3 Gb in 1,805 contigs, with 56,354 annotated genes and 98.5% complete BUSCOs. Agalinis fasciculata is resolved into 14 pseudochromosomes spanning 2.29 Gb from HiFi and Omni-C data. The novelty lies in applying these standards to a tetraploid tuber crop and a haplotype-resolved fungal pair.
